title: Siri AI on iPhone: Who Gets It, English Only, and How to Turn It On
description:
You already have ChatGPT and Gemini on your phone, so why is Apple replacing Siri with Siri AI? This video compares the three assistants side by side, then follows Apple's official pages to explain who can use Siri AI, how to turn it on, and which of your data it reads.
For anyone who saw the "Siri is switching to Gemini" news and wants to know whether their iPhone gets it.

It covers how each of the three assistants gets your personal data, Siri AI's four abilities, supported devices, English-only support and the waitlist for now, the exceptions for the EU and mainland China, what Apple says about Private Cloud Compute, and the daily usage limits. Feature descriptions are each company's own claims, and this site has no Siri AI account. To see how the three assistants split everyday tasks, read our article "Three AI Assistants Compared: Same Tasks and Scoring Method".

chapters.three-assistants: Siri AI vs ChatGPT vs Gemini

w2hp.text: You already have ChatGPT and Gemini on your phone, so why a new Siri?

45ma.text: You'd think it's just one more chatty assistant.

ne2s.text: The gap is data: Apple says it directly understands personal context.

qher.text: Apple's support page lists at least these five sources.

6gqm.text: So how do the three assistants compare?

4edf.text: First, one table: how each assistant gets your data.

dtqw.text: Siri AI lives in the OS; Apple says it understands your messages and mail.

fg87.text: In ChatGPT, you connect the services you want it to read in settings.

swab.text: Same for Gemini: you pick which services to connect.

6trj.text: Once connected, they all act for you, but what connects depends on plan, region and device.

w9na.text: Key last column: Siri AI is English-only for now; the other two work in Chinese.

zpue.text: To be clear, these are each company's own claims, and I haven't tried Siri AI.

32wr.text: My view: not who's smarter, but how much data it reads and whether you control it.

whws.text: So what can Siri AI itself actually do?

2pmv.text: Apple splits the new Siri's abilities into four parts.

9s7f.text: First, personal context: it finds info across messages, mail and calendar.

zu7v.text: Second, world knowledge: when it needs fresh information, it searches the web.

hs8t.text: Third, screen awareness: it answers about or acts on what's on screen.

ni9m.text: Fourth, system app actions, like sending messages or adding events.

rzsw.text: In short: a Siri that can look things up, see your screen, and take action.

xpfc.text: Apple's own examples below, not our tests.

vtb4.text: Ask what family said they'd do together when visiting.

ytij.text: It finds in messages: baking a family recipe together.

e5m8.text: Then it pulls the recipe from Mail and adds ingredients to a Reminders list.

kb2a.text: You're viewing a team's website and say: add the home games to my calendar.

ej7r.text: It reads the schedule on screen and adds those games directly.

nfk4.text: There's also a standalone Siri app this time.

upkw.text: It syncs conversations through iCloud, like a chat history.

kk46.text: Start on your phone, and continue on another device.

cmby.text: Three ways to invoke new Siri.

emx3.text: Besides saying Hey Siri, hold the side button.

5ctn.text: Or swipe down from the Dynamic Island and just talk.

2h9b.text: All three lead to the same new Siri.

b8bk.text: Ask the same thing to the other two assistants, and it differs.

vypt.text: Siri AI is a system-level entry point; Apple says it directly understands personal context.

jep2.text: ChatGPT and Gemini are separate apps; finding your data relies on connected services.

5ac9.text: One lives in the system, two in apps, so their roles differ.

f9ga.text: So can your phone actually use it?

w293.text: First, is your device eligible? Apple lists them.

zvte.text: iPhone: 15 Pro series, 16 series or later, or iPhone Air.

rq8n.text: iPad and Mac have their own cutoffs, mostly newer models with Apple silicon.

fedb.text: And it needs an iPhone with Siri AI on.

n4yd.text: Older models not on the list won't get Siri AI this time.

b74t.text: This device table is the first gate to using it.

jedh.text: Next, language, which I think is Taiwan users' biggest tradeoff.

af4g.text: French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish: Apple said on September 14 they join in October.

6jei.text: Also not offered under age 13; Apple states this too.

m823.text: ChatGPT and Gemini work in Chinese right now, unlike Siri AI.

4xkv.text: In the EU, Siri AI isn't offered on iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch.

uicr.text: Mac and Vision Pro work in English.

3ssf.text: Apple Accounts set to mainland China don't work for now.

gihf.text: Beyond language, Apple requires an account in an eligible region.

rske.text: But the support document gives no list, nor says whether Taiwan is included.

38x4.text: For Taiwan accounts, go by Apple's site; I won't guess.

yn3w.text: Because device language and Siri language must match.

f32x.text: To use Siri AI now, switch your whole iPhone to English.

a8gr.text: Whether it handles Chinese messages well once set to English, Apple hasn't said.

f9ab.text: Apple hasn't said when Traditional Chinese comes; go by its site.

td52.text: So if you really want to try it, how do you sign up?

mzk3.text: Grab your iPhone and let's turn it on, step by step.

cv6w.text: Step one: update your system to iOS 27.

r7ce.text: Step two: open Settings, tap Siri, and if it's off, turn it on first.

k94g.text: Step three: on the same page, tap Try Siri AI (Beta).

f2y4.text: Step four: pick a voice, finish voice setup.

yafh.text: Step five: review privacy settings, more next chapter.

wam6.text: After these five steps, your request is sent; the hard part is the wait.

kj9e.text: The big misunderstanding: tapping it doesn't mean instant access.

cz4u.text: Apple puts you on a waitlist; the wait time varies.

89ef.text: At your turn, Siri AI downloads automatically.

48zx.text: Others may already use it, but yours may not be ready.

nhbr.text: So before it's enabled, what should you check in privacy settings?

qxih.text: Convenience means reading your data, so check what it reads.

ar63.text: Messages, mail, calendar, notes and reminders are all included.

riw5.text: It also sees what's on your screen now.

jamr.text: The more it reads, the handier, so know what it reads.

4azm.text: Where is data processed? Apple says on-device plus Private Cloud Compute.

hu63.text: It says personal data isn't stored in processing and Apple can't access it.

paui.text: And outside experts can verify that promise at any time.

h83z.text: The new model was built together with Google and its Gemini.

4pyb.text: All of this is Apple's account, and we can't independently verify it.

3dey.text: Another angle: what can you decide yourself?

vh8m.text: Siri AI has you review privacy settings when you enable it.

u8jx.text: ChatGPT and Gemini: you pick which accounts to connect, and can disconnect anytime.

d2h9.text: My view: the less you connect, and the clearer it is, the safer it feels.

4bj2.text: Apple says server-dependent features have daily usage limits, and Siri AI is one of them.

fa3w.text: Paid options for more usage are planned later.

9gfn.text: It's beta too: answers may be wrong, rules may change.

7i8m.text: Treat it as still in testing, and expect accordingly.

9z2v.text: So when enabling, read the privacy settings; don't just keep pressing Next.

96fq.text: Full article: top of the description.

c2t9.text: After all this, is it worth switching to English for it?

unw2.text: Back to start: with ChatGPT and Gemini, do you need Siri AI?

a2rk.text: First: it lives in the system, the others in apps.

v485.text: Second: English-only for now, so the whole device must switch.

rape.text: Third: after applying you wait on a list, then it downloads.

7qte.text: My answer: because it lives in the system, not because it's smarter.

egzt.text: If you mainly use Chinese, the other two assistants work in Chinese now.

jvk4.text: Apple hasn't said when Siri AI gets Traditional Chinese; go by its site.

2zay.text: See which ability you use daily, then decide whether to try it now.

n5af.text: Finding your own data, asking about the screen, or acting across apps?

w3v9.text: For how the three split daily tasks, see our article Three AI Assistants Compared.
